sections.title: Origins & History
sections.text: The Sun Temple at Konark, on the coast of Odisha in the Puri district, is a 13th century monument designed as a colossal chariot of the sun god Surya. It was built around 1250 by the Eastern Ganga king Narasimhadeva I, and is one of the high points of Kalinga architecture. Its position facing the Bay of Bengal, where the rising sun strikes the temple, was chosen deliberately. European sailors once called it the Black Pagoda because the tall tower, a landmark for ships, appeared dark from the sea.

sections.title: Beauty & Atmosphere
sections.text: The beauty of Konark lies in its sculpture and its concept. The temple is imagined as a giant stone chariot with twelve pairs of finely carved wheels and seven galloping horses. The wheels are about three metres across and also work as sundials, which can show the time of day when the shadow falls on the spokes. Every surface is carved with detail, from floral patterns and mythical beasts to dancers, musicians, elephants and scenes of court life. Some panels include the famous erotic sculptures, which form a small part of the artwork.

sections.title: Architecture & Highlights
sections.text: The original great tower, said to have been about 70 metres high, collapsed in the 19th century, but the Jagamohana, or assembly hall, still stands in great grandeur with its tiered roof. In front is the Natya Mandapa, the hall of dance, with beautiful carving, and the sun god's images face different directions to catch the sun at morning, noon and evening. The temple is built of khondalite, laterite and chlorite stone.

sections.title: Famous For
sections.text: Konark was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1984. It is famous as a masterpiece of Odisha's temple architecture and a symbol of the state, and a representation of it has appeared on Indian currency. Each December, the Konark Dance Festival is staged in an open-air theatre near the temple.

visitor_tips: Visitors should go early in the morning or late afternoon for softer light, and plan about two hours.
Puri, with the Jagannath Temple, and Bhubaneswar are close by, and Chandrabhaga Beach is a short drive.
